today.name: TheySaid 4.0
today.tagline: See how users will react, right where you build.
today.description: Put what you’re building in front of real customers or synthetic users trained on them when you need an answer in minutes without leaving Claude, Cursor, or Jira. Nothing ships on a guess.
today.category: User Experience • Artificial Intelligence • UX Design
today.categoryFa: User Experience • هوش مصنوعی • UX Design

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt 👋I’m Chris, co-founder of TheySaid. Years ago I built the original UserTesting, so I’ve spent most of my career helping teams watch real people use their products.Here’s what changed: your team now ships more decisions than ever (designs, tickets, PRs), but checking them with customers still means scheduling, recruiting, and waiting. So it gets skipped. We call the result Validation Debt: the cost of decisions you shipped without customer evidence.TheySaid 4.0 lets you see how users will react, right where you build. Ask from Claude Design, v0, Replit, Bolt or Lovable, or have it run automatically when a Jira, Linear, ClickUp or Monday ticket finishes design. Then watch real people or synthetic users try what you just made.What’s new:Synthetic users: that actually use your product, on screen and out loud. Each starts from a model trained on 100,000+ hours of real usability sessions, then is tuned to your customers with the data you choose: call recordings, surveys, support tickets, CRM.Audiences: define your real and synthetic customer groups once, and anyone in your org can reuse them.MCP + Ticket Testing: feedback and a fix-it prompt inside your build tools, plus validation that triggers itself when design is done. No one has to remember to ask.AI Companion: tell it what you need, and it does the work.Experience Hub: always-on scoring of your critical customer experiences, with what to fix next.Skills: reusable prompts for summaries, cohort analysis, and reports. Build it once. Run it forever.Plus mobile app testing, clips and highlight reels, screeners, response quality monitoring, a unified test builder, a redesigned UI, and more.Stop shipping decisions nobody validated. 🚫Try 4.0 FREE → https://www.theysaid.io/v4And tell me: when you build with AI today, how do you find out whether customers get it? Or do you skip that step?

Very cool use of AI - we're pushing new features daily and getting a real user test on those is always tricky. Our current customers do bring up the issues they want fixed to begin with. Is there a way to tune TheySaid on a new customer audience that we're targeting rather than just our current customers? I.e., for a new feature that reaches a different niche? And if so, how would that type of tuning be done?

The part I keep coming back to is the audience answering and asking questions as if they are talking to you, after training in under a minute from a URL or internal doc. Do the questions the synthetic users ask back get surfaced separately from the usability feedback? That feels like the more useful signal to me — a tester asking about something missing usually points at a gap in the doc or the onboarding itself, rather than just a confusing screen. And when a question goes beyond what was in the URL or doc, does the tester say so, or does it answer from general knowledge?

Hey @chrishicken and team Congrats on the launch :) Lovely product I would say as I believe synthetic testers that think aloud while recording their screen is a actually a smart idea. Specially when so many new builders shipping fast with AI, most don't have a user base to test with yet, so being able to see where people would hesitate or drop off before launch is big thing for them.Congrats on launch again and best wishes ahead 😄
Looks promising! I'd definitely use that to get some feedback on users flows. Good job team!
Hi, team congrats. very curious how Synthetic users get created? is there any metrics showing the accuracy of simulation?

"Validation Debt" is a great name for it. As a solo maker who launched today, I know how easy that step is to skip. Question about the synthetic users: does a test tell you how confident it is, or flag when a result should be checked with real people? For a niche B2B audience I'd trust a synthetic "this flow is confusing" more than a synthetic "I'd pay for this".
Having a ticket finishing design in Jira or Linear trigger a synthetic test on its own is a handy idea. how do you keep the synthetic users from just agreeing with everything?

today.name: Orbit
today.tagline: Stop doomscrolling. Earn every app unlock.
today.description: Doomscrolling is free. Orbit makes it cost something. Pick a schedule and your apps lock themselves. Want back in early? Earn it: hold the orb, do squats, ask a friend, pay a little more each time, or win a shift at The Gate. Most times, you’ll stay out.

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt 👋I’m Alara, one of the builders and the head marketer of Orbit!Last month, my Screen Time report said 10h 19m a day. More than 80% of it was doomscrolling. I was a full-on blue light zombie: in bed at 1 AM, saying “just one more video,” waking up tired. Finally I asked myself, what am I doing with my life??I tried every digital detox trick. Deleting apps only to reinstall them in the next hour 😅. Grayscale mode. A “dopamine detox” weekend. Strict blockers I learned to bypass in two taps.That last one showed us the real problem: getting back in was free. One tap and I was scrolling again. So we built Orbit around one idea: every unlock should cost you something.🔒 Pick a schedule (No scroll till evening, Deep work mornings, Sleep) and your apps lock on their own🏋️ Still want in? Earn it:• Hold the orb and breathe• Do squats in front of the camera, or play a head-movement game• Ask a friend. Your accountability partner gets the request and says yes or no• Pay: $0.99, then $1.99, up to $9.99 that week. Or send it to a nonprofit instead• Work a night shift at The Gate Inc.: judge 8 residents’ requests to go online. Make 2 mistakes or fewer, and you earn your break. Only 3 shifts a day, so the game never becomes the new feed (My personal favorite)👯 Together: lock a whole group’s phones at once, for dinner, a study night or a tripA month later: 10h 19m → 6h 14m a day. My social media time? Cut in half. No phone in bed means no blue light before sleep, and I sleep noticeably better.The research points the same way:• 1 in 9 teens across 44 countries now show signs of social media addiction, up from 1 in 14 in 2018 (WHO/HBSC)• In a 2025 randomized trial, blocking mobile internet for just 2 weeks improved attention, mental health and well-being; over 90% of participants improved on at least one (PNAS Nexus)This math is making me scared: at 10 hours a day, the next decade would have cost me 4+ years of waking life.I’d love to know: what would stop you faster: 20 squats, asking your mom, or $9.99? 😅Feel free to use 20% discounts special for this launch:20% OFF on annual plan PHA2020% OFF on lifetime plan PHL20
This is a cool. I knew a friend of mine actually built toys for kids to earn screen time by actually doing house chores. Similar ideas. bet they work really well. congrats!
Is this app good for teens? You mention some stats on that, and would love to somehow get my tween on board. But how to motivate him with this app?

Nice launch Orhan. Capping The Gate at three shifts a day is a small rule with a big effect, otherwise the mini-game just becomes the new feed. For the people who stuck with it past week one, which unlock path do they actually use most: friend approval, squats, or pay?

I am sad to admit that I do need this product to help me overcome my scrolling habit. I think the way the app works is quite unique and intuitive. When you say that I have to pay to do something, I would rather stick to what I am supposed to do. I think this is a great way to make me more serious about leaving this habit behind. However, sometimes I just go with the flow, so even if I agree to text someone and close the app, my muscle memory might still lead me to start scrolling. How would this be detected, and how would such a situation be handled?

Nice idea and much needed for us all nowadays.Question: a lot of these apps are needed for tasks that are not doomscrolling (e.g. replying a to a friend's message) -> is there a way/thought on how you can account for that? e.g. something like detect on the app when the attention drifts from 'real tasks' to 'doom scrolling'?

Honest answer to your question: paying would stop me fastest. The tricky part for me is that half my scrolling is actually work, since I run Instagram for two brands. Does the "What for?" prompt let you save a reason like "replying to DMs," so work sessions don't eat into the limit?
The group lock for dinner is a fun idea. Can everyone choose which apps to block, or does the whole group use the same settings?

today.name: Spacesheep
today.tagline: Documents of the future, made by AI, read by your team
today.description: Spacesheep (YC F26) turns any agent's work into a space: an interactive doc, live dashboard, mockup or app. Share it with specific people, your team or publicly, and collaborate on it together.

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt, I'm Michael, founder of Spacesheep (YC F26).Agentic output is growing, while our ability to read remains the same.With Spacesheep you can turn any agentic output into a visual space. Share it with colleagues, comment on the exact line, or add an integration and stream live data into it (see examples below).How it works:1. Ask the AI you already use: "Use spacesheep.dev and give a visual explanation of how GPUs work."2. You get a space: a document, a mockup, a dashboard, an app or art.3. Share it with specific people, your team, or publicly. Write @​spacesheep in a comment, and the AI fixes the space while everyone watches. Every version is kept.It works with any agent: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, ChatGPT, Grok, Grok Build and open-source harnesses like opencode. Or use Spacesheep's own AI on the dashboard, in Slack and more. Every space syncs to your own Google Drive or GitHub.Examples:- YC by the numbers, made by an agent: https://spacesheep.dev/@misha/yc-by-the-numbers- A live thermal camera streaming into a space: https://spacesheep.dev/@yaroslavvb/thermal-master-p3-live-camera-stream- An interactive map of the ET-SoC-1 chip: https://spacesheep.dev/@yaroslavvb/et-soc1-chip-diagram- An AI Foundry lab dashboard: https://spacesheep.dev/@yaroslavvb/aifoundry-lab-dashboardVideos:- Launch video: https://youtu.be/cFVCDSs-GZs- Spacesheep in 90 seconds: https://youtu.be/vKQtOTrRBBA- How James Briggs uses it with Claude Code: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lJVcc4O-7ckWhy I'm building it: https://spacesheep.dev/whyIt's free to start. We would love any feedback and ideas!

Some constructive feedback: it took almost 30 seconds for your video to show what your product was, and I lost interest. Product feedback: 1. I don't understand what this actually does compared to something like Claude Artifacts; it seems like your only advantage is cross-platform compatibility. 2. Most of your examples look like the walls of text your tool promises to eliminate. What is the intended medium to "cut down on walls of text"?Not trying to be negative for nothing; I just want to understand your thoughts.

The GitHub sync is the part I'm most curious about. When a space syncs to GitHub, what actually lands in the repo — is the space stored as files a teammate could open and edit there, or is GitHub more of a snapshot/backup while the live editing stays in Spacesheep?
Tagging @spacesheep in a comment so the AI fixes the doc while everyone watches is a fun touch 🐑 can you roll back to an older version if the fix goes sideways?
Whoa! Can't wait to try it. So many of us are visual learners and can sometimes process a higher volume of information, and more quickly, than by reading.

Turning an agent run into something a teammate can actually open and click through instead of a wall of chat logs is the missing step, and sharing it with just two people instead of the whole workspace is the detail I appreciate.

As a copywriter, I always found Google Docs quite static. Notion was exciting, but Spacesheep feels like the perfect place for an AI-powered copy editing workflow. I am already thinking of the use cases like generating a landing page, campaign concept, or messaging one-pager with the copy and visuals in one place, then let stakeholders comment directly on the exact headline or CTA they want changed. Asking the AI to revise just that line, without rewriting the whole page. The versioning is the part I’d use most. Ad and landing-page copy lives or dies by small wording changes, so being able to compare drafts and keep the strongest version instead of losing it in ChatGPT’s history would save a lot of back-and-forth.Lastly, the pricing would definitely invite adoption from teams of all sizes. Congrats Michael!
Congratulations on being selected for Y Combinator. 🙂What's the most unexpected or creative use case of space you have seen so far??

today.name: SavorApp_AI
today.tagline: Capture what matters and move your intentions forward
today.description: Savor is an Intention Layer™ for thoughts that never reach your to-do list. Speak, type, or snap a photo to create a clear card in Now, Soon, or Later. Reminders bring it back when it matters. Take Action (Beta) helps you explore options, build a plan or list, and draft words you can use. Review and adjust as you go. Hand off a card or a single step, with a private chat for context. You decide what happens next. Free on iOS and Android.

comments.text: Hi Product Hunt. I’m Lana, and I built Savor because of the thoughts that never make it anywhere.When we interviewed early users, everyone had a system for the big things: a calendar, an inbox, a to-do list. What they did not have was a place for the other ten percent: the hallway conversation, the flyer on the fridge, the podcast someone mentioned. Those lived in their heads, and came back at midnight.How it worksSpeak, type, or snap a bill, letter, or flyer.Savor shapes it into a clear card: what it is, when it matters, what to do next.Cards sit in Now, Soon, or Later.They come back with reminders you control.What makes it differentHand off a card or a single step to someone else, with a private chat for context. Once they accept, they become its editor and receive its reminders. You keep a read-only copy and can take it back. No streaks, badges, or scores.A few things to tryPhotograph a bill so its details do not get lost.Capture someone you meant to call or a place a friend recommended.Hand a card to your partner instead of carrying it alone.Use voice capture, a Siri shortcut on iPhone, or add a card to your calendar.We call this an Intention Layer™: a place for things while they are still becoming something.Try it free on iPhone and Android.Which thought would you give Savor first? I’d love to hear what feels useful and what it gets wrong.

Handing off just one step with its own private chat is the detail that caught my eye too. When someone accepts that step, do they only see that step and its chat, or can they see the rest of the card as well? I'm curious how you draw that line, especially for the more personal cards.

We're aware that if it's too long people will skip it but then they may not know about some of SAVOR's more powerful features under the hood. But if we make the onboarding shorter and quicker, then many of those more powerful features are still undiscovered. We're super curious to hear the community's thoughts and opinions.

today.name: PulseDev
today.tagline: Click any UI bug on localhost and your AI agent fixes it
today.description: Stop describing UI bugs to your AI. Click any element on your localhost site, say what's wrong, and Claude Code, Codex, Gemini or OpenCode edits the right file. Watch it work live, then approve the diff on the page. Nothing is written until you do.

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt 👋“The button below the second pricing card. No, the other one.”When you’re building a website with a coding agent, you can see what needs changing: a button that doesn’t line up, a heading that wraps awkwardly, or spacing that feels off. But getting that change made means turning what you see into a text prompt.You explain where the element is. Open DevTools. Copy a selector or take a screenshot. Find the component. Switch to the terminal, paste everything in, and hope you’ve given the agent enough context. Then go back to the browser to check the result.For a small visual change, explaining the task can feel like more work than the change itself. And when there are several things to fix, you repeat that process for each one.I was already looking at the bug. I just wanted to click it.That’s why I built PulseDev: to give your coding agent the context behind the element you’re pointing at, alongside your instructions.From “which button?” to “make this button taller”Click the element on your local site and describe what you want changed. PulseDev attaches the selected element’s context, including its selector and styles. The Vite plugin adds source mapping where supported, helping the agent locate the relevant code.You still decide what the change should be. PulseDev handles the handoff from the page to your agent.How it worksOpen your local site in your browser and click an element. Shift-click to select more than one.Describe the change: “Match this button’s height to the one beside it.”Send it to Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI or OpenCode and follow the agent’s activity beside the page.Review the proposed diff in your browser. Approve or reject it in review mode, or enable auto-apply when you want it.Built for the tools you already usePulseDev works with your own browser, local project and installed coding agent. Add the widget with a script tag, or use the Vite plugin for source mapping where supported. Your agent’s usual usage limits and provider charges still apply.It’s for the UI work that adds up: adjusting spacing, matching styles between elements, changing copy, and polishing the details before you ship.Free for one project on macOS. Pro unlocks unlimited projects. Subscribe before November 3, 2026 for $12/month and keep that rate. New subscriptions are $18/month from November 3. No promo code needed.I’d love to hear about your workflow- Think about the last UI change you asked a coding agent to make. What was harder: explaining which element you meant, or getting the change right?- How do you share UI context today—screenshots, selectors, file paths, or descriptions?- What would you need to see before trusting the proposed change?- After trying PulseDev, where did you still have to explain yourself?
Nothing is written until you approve, love that.I'd never let an agent touch files without seeing diffs first.

Thanks to everyone who flagged that our download page said PulseDev isn't code-signed. That was leftover copy from the beta and it's now fixed. PulseDev of course is signed with our Apple Developer ID and notarized by Apple, so macOS opens it without any warning or Terminal workaround. We really appreciate you pointing it out!
Quick q: is it Mac only for now? I'm on Windows most days and the free plan says one project on macOS. Clicking the element instead of describing it to Claude is the bit I'd pay for.

The diff review in the browser is the part that would make me actually use this — I don't want an agent editing files from a screenshot description. I'm curious what the agent gets when there's no Vite source mapping: just the selector and computed styles, or does it still try to resolve the component? That's usually where 'make this match that' falls apart for me.
does it work with frameworks other than vite, like next.js? or is it mostly the script tag there?
I've been describing the same localhost bug to Claude three different ways this week. The click-to-fix loop here is exactly the shorthand I didn't know I needed.
Shift-clicking two elements is a small detail I like. For 'make this match that', being able to point at both gets rid of a lot of explaining.

yesterday.name: Strawberry 1.0
yesterday.tagline: AI Browser that saves your team >100h/week
yesterday.description: Strawberry is an AI browser that can do hours of work in minutes. Strawberry's agents, which we call "Companions", can research hundreds of leads in parallel, transcribe your meetings, automate follow-ups, and handle all the repetitive admin your team keeps procrastinating. Create or hire a pre-made companion, teach it your preferences and share it with your whole team. Hundreds of teams, including Lovable, Tandem Health and ElevenLabs, already use Strawberry.

comments.text: Hi everyone! Charles here, and I'm really excited to share Strawberry 1.0 with you 🍓A year ago we launched our beta here on Product Hunt. Back then, Strawberry was a simple browser with a built-in AI agent.Today it's a fully fledged agent platform that hundreds of teams, including Lovable, Tandem Health and ElevenLabs, use to run agents around the clock, transcribe meetings and build a shared company context.We call these agents "companions".🫠 The problemDevelopers already have great AI agents that can work for hours on end, like Claude Code and Codex. But those tools are built for people who work in files, not tabs. These apps are powerful, but usually too complex for the average non-technical team.Newer assistants like Dots, Grok Bot and Instinct are much more delightful and intuitive, and they're great for consumers. But they're hard to rely on for real team work. You mostly work through one long chat and can't easily see what the agent is doing.🌐 Why we built a browserThe browser strikes the perfect balance between intuitive and powerful.Everyone knows how to use a browser, and it's where most of your team's work already happens. Your tools, your context and your logins are all there. The browser as the interface makes it much easier for e.g. sales, marketing and talent teams to get started with agents, while still being possible to build advanced systems that run on their own.We're also big believers in the agentic web. Soon there will be trillions of AI agents communicating and trading with each other. comments.text: Hi everyone, I'm Elle, and I work on product and go-to-market for zCAD. The question we kept coming back to: where is this model going to live? If it lives in a game, a render or a virtual world, a mesh is the right answer, and AI 3D tools already do it well. If it has to work in the physical world, fit another part, take a screw, get printed or machined, it needs CAD: real dimensions, solid geometry, parts that mate. zCAD. AI generates that from a prompt, and exports STEP into the tool you already use.On the product side, a few choices are deliberate. Even the free plan exports STEP, because a part you can't take into your own tools isn't really yours. We turn down figurine requests, because sculpted, organic shapes are what mesh does best, even when you print them. And it doesn't make engineering calls for you. Tolerances and materials stay with you. On the go-to-market side, I'll be honest: we're still learning who needs this most. Makers who 3D print, indie hardware designers, engineers who live in CAD all day? That's a big part of why we're here. Try it on something that has to work in the real world, and tell us who you are and where it breaks.

Each agent is fast on its own, but they can't talk to each other, so you become the go-between. week.aiReview:
مسئله و راه‌حل:
بزرگ‌ترین چالش توسعه مبتنی بر ایجنت‌های چندگانه، تبدیل شدن انسان به «مدیر پروژه» یا واسط خسته‌کننده انتقال اطلاعات (Context) بین جلسات کاری مختلف است. BAND با ارائه یک فضای کاری مشترک (Shared Workspace/Room)، امکان ارتباط مستقیم، پیام‌دهی، اشتراک‌گذاری حافظه و تحویل کار بین ایجنت‌های مختلف (مانند Copilot، Claude و Codex) را بدون تغییر ابزار اصلی توسعه‌دهنده فراهم می‌کند.

معماری و تکنولوژی:
ساختار سیستم بر پایه الگوریتم‌های مدیریت حالت (State Management) متمرکز و پروتکل‌های ارتباطی در زمان‌واقعی (Real-time WebSockets) بنا شده است. حافظه مشترک در سطح «اتاق» ذخیره می‌شود تا با بستن یک جلسه کاری، زمینه پروژه از بین نرود.

مدل درآمدی:
مدل فری‌میوم با نرم‌افزار دسکتاپ رایگان برای کاربران فردی و مدل اشتراکی SaaS برای تیم‌ها جهت استفاده از فضاهای کاری ابری مشترک، مدیریت دسترسی‌ها و حافظه طولانی‌مدت ایجنت‌ها.

نقاط قوت:
۱. عدم نیاز به تغییر IDE یا ابزارهای موجود توسعه‌دهنده.
۲. حفظ زمینه (Context Persistence) مستقل از جلسات کاری فردی.
۳. کاهش چشمگیر دخالت انسانی در فرآیند تحویل کارهای خرد.

نقاط ضعف:
۱. خطر تعارض ایجنت‌ها و ابطال اشتباه کارهای یکدیگر در صورت مدیریت نامناسب زمینه.
۲. پیچیدگی همگام‌سازی سریع روی چند دستگاه مختلف.

نکته طلایی برای بازار ایران:
بزرگ‌ترین ارزش این ابزار برای تیم‌های ایرانی، کاهش هزینه‌های Onboarding و حفظ دانش فنی پروژه است. پیاده‌سازی پلتفرمی مشابه که بتواند مدلسازی حافظه بومی و اتصال به ایجنت‌های متن‌باز (Open-Source) سفارشی‌سازی‌شده را روی زیرساخت داخلی مدیریت کند، بازار بسیار جذابی در میان شرکت‌های نرم‌افزاری ایران خواهد داشت.

week.name: MOVO AI
week.tagline: The world's first long-form video agent for mobile
week.description: MOVO AI is the world’s first AI video agent for long-form creation that works right from your phone. It also works on the web. Shoot, upload, or start with an idea, then tell MOVO AI what you want. MOVO plans, creates, refines, keeps characters and scenes consistent, and brings the whole video together. Lock your phone and MOVO keeps working. Come back to review or make changes through chat. No prompt gymnastics. No canvas-heavy workflows. No manual clip stitching.

comments.text: Hi Product Hunt 👋I’m one of the makers behind MOVO AI—the world’s first long-form video agent on your mobile.My mother is a small creator who manages several social media accounts, and my father is her loyal cameraman. They are both over 60, but they still spend hours filming, editing, posting, and proudly watching every new like and follower.They make little, if any, money from it. But social media gives them something real: an audience, confidence, and the feeling that their stories are being seen.At the same time, I watched more founders around me become creators. They recorded videos between meetings, explained their ideas to customers, and built influence around themselves and their products.I was different. I was an introverted engineer who began working in AI while completing my graduate degree at Carnegie Mellon University. I had ideas, but I didn’t understand camera movements, editing, or how to look natural on camera. Even with the newest iPhone, I often didn’t know where to begin.My parents showed me how meaningful it could be to share your life. The founders around me showed me how necessary video was becoming. Together, they made me feel like I was being left behind by an era I was helping to build.That gap became the reason we built MOVO AI.What is MOVO?MOVO turns an idea into a complete long-form video through one continuous conversation.Start with a rough thought, script, reference, or a few assets. MOVO helps structure the story, establish the characters and visual direction, generate scenes, respond to feedback, and compose everything into a cohesive video.You don’t need to know the technical name of every shot or write a complex prompt for each scene. You can simply talk to MOVO as you would talk to a director, creative partner, or friend.Internally, we describe it as “Codex for video”: you direct what you want to create without writing every underlying instruction yourself.What surprised usWe initially thought eliminating prompt gymnastics would mainly help beginners. Professional AI creators already knew how to write sophisticated prompts, select models, and manage complicated workflows.We underestimated how much professionals would value this approach too.They embraced it not because they couldn’t write prompts, but because they wanted to focus their attention on what matters more: story, structure, pacing, characters, and emotion.Conversations with accomplished professors and screenwriters at USC’s School of Cinematic Arts reinforced this belief. Models and production tools will keep changing, but storytelling remains the foundation.We realized that agentic creation is not simply an easier mode for beginners. It may be a more universal creative interface: accessible enough for a first-time creator, yet powerful enough to free professionals from repetitive production work.Why mobile mattersOnce creation becomes conversational, it no longer needs to live inside a desktop canvas.A founder can start a product video before the next meeting. A store owner can review an advertisement from behind the counter. A parent can develop a family story in the park. A filmmaker can approve scenes while moving between locations. A hiker can capture an idea at the summit before the inspiration disappears.You might describe an idea over breakfast, approve the storyboard on the train, review generated scenes after work, and refine the ending before bed.MOVO continues working asynchronously, so you don’t need to babysit every generation. Creation can move with your life instead of requiring your life to stop.From one video to an ongoing worldWithin the same project, you can begin Episodes 2, 3, and 4 in new sessions without re-entering the same characters, products, locations, and creative direction.MOVO carries that context forward, helping you develop an ongoing world rather than a collection of disconnected clips.What we’d love you to testWe would especially value feedback on three things:Does talking to MOVO feel like working with a useful director or creative partner?Can you meaningfully develop a video on mobile without supervising every step?How well does MOVO preserve your creative world across multiple episodes?AI video still has many unsolved problems, and MOVO is still evolving. We want to hear where it understands your direction, where it surprises you, and where it falls short.Our goal is not to replace human creativity. It is to close the gap between having a story and being able to show it.Anyone with a story should be able to make it move—wherever life takes them.Your idea. Moved by MOVO. 🎬

Full disclosure — I'm a big fan of Anthropic and actually built an app that works exclusively with Claude Desktop for secure local file search. So I've spent a lot of time thinking about this space.My concern with Cowork isn't the vision, it's the architecture. Agentic tasks burn through tokens fast (Anthropic says so themselves), so that $200/month cap can disappear quicker than you'd expect. And at that price, you'd want to use it for real work — but the whole thing requires giving Claude direct read/write/delete access to your files. If you're handling client data, patient records, or anything regulated, you're basically out.The bigger issue is prompt injection. Anthropic admits "the chances of an attack are still non-zero" — and back in October 2025, researchers showed exactly that: a prompt injection against Claude that pulled up to 30MB of user data per request through Anthropic's own API. When you're talking about an agent with file system access, email connectors, and a browser, that's not some theoretical edge case.There's a reason some of us build tools where Claude can search your files without actually touching them. The agentic future is definitely coming, but "AI that can access everything" and "AI that keeps you in control" are two very different products for two very different users.
